entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.025 establishing production, barreling, and Missouri-grown corn standards for labeling Missouri bourbon.

headings.title: Criteria for Missouri bourbon labeling
headings.reviewNote: Requires a spirit labeled as Missouri bourbon or Missouri bourbon whiskey to be mashed, fermented, distilled, aged, and bottled in Missouri in Missouri-manufactured oak barrels.

headings.title: Missouri-grown corn requirement beginning 2020
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that beginning January 1, 2020, all corn used in the mash of Missouri bourbon must be Missouri-grown corn.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 311.028 governing Ozark Highlands spirits standards, single malt certification, guild seals, and DNR regional mapping.

headings.title: Ozark Highlands spirits qualification requirements
headings.reviewNote: Establishes production, aging, barreling, and natural spring water criteria for aged and unaged spirits labeled as Ozark Highlands spirits.

headings.title: Single malt qualification at single distillery
headings.reviewNote: Requires products qualifying as Single Malt to be distilled and bottled at a single distillery.

headings.title: Certification by distillers guild
headings.reviewNote: Requires qualifying Ozark Highlands spirits to be certified by seal or other means by the Ozark Highland Distillers Guild.

headings.title: Official regional map publication
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of natural resources, in collaboration with the guild, to produce and publish an official map of the Ozark Highlands region.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.055 governing homebrewing license exemptions, household production limits, removal for events, and non-sale status.

headings.title: Manufacturing exemption for personal or family use
headings.reviewNote: Exempts individuals aged 21 and older from manufacturing licensing for personal or family use up to statutory volume limits, prohibiting commercial sale.

headings.title: Removal of homebrewed beer for organized events
headings.reviewNote: Permits removing homebrewed beer from brewing premises for personal or family use, including organized events, exhibitions, or competitions, off licensed premises or at specified temporary/tax-exempt premises (source footnote notes 'sections' in original rolls).

headings.title: Admission-fee events not deemed sale of beer
headings.reviewNote: Provides that homebrewed beer served without separate charge at paid admission events is not deemed a sale if the brewer receives no proceeds.

entries.reviewSummary: Qualifications for individual, partnership, and corporate liquor licenses, unrelated-felony employee protection, resident corporation and financial interest definitions, sworn statements, and five-year post-revocation eligibility.

headings.title: General applicant and managing officer qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Requires good moral character, qualified legal voter, and taxpaying citizen status for individual applicants and corporate managing officers, bars revoked licensees and post-21st Amendment liquor-law violators, and permits nonresident/foreign corporation wholesaler sales.

headings.title: Disqualifications, unrelated-felony rule, and resident wholesalers
headings.reviewNote: Bars licenses where 10%+ owners, officers, or employees have revocations or liquor-law convictions, prohibits penalizing licenses solely for an employee's unrelated felony, and restricts over-5% wholesaler licenses to resident corporations.

headings.title: Definition of resident corporation and grandfather clause
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'resident corporation' requiring Missouri incorporation, qualified officers/directors, and 60% resident-owned stock/voting/financial interest (three-year state residency), with a January 1, 1947 grandfather exception.

headings.title: Definition of financial interest
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'financial interest' broadly to encompass all direct or indirect legal or beneficial interests in capital or net profits of the licensed enterprise, excluding ordinary commercial or bona fide bank credit.

headings.title: Sworn applicant statements and reporting material changes
headings.reviewNote: Directs the supervisor by regulation to require sworn written statements from license applicants, including residency of financially interested persons for wholesalers and retailers, and requires prompt reporting of material changes.

headings.title: Employee eligibility five years after license revocation
headings.reviewNote: Makes any person whose chapter 311 license or permit was revoked automatically eligible to work as an employee of a licensed establishment five years after revocation.

headings.title: Reapplication for new license five years after revocation
headings.reviewNote: Makes revoked licensees eligible to apply for a new license or permit five years after revocation at ATC's discretion, with a five-year bar after denial and administrative hearing commission review under section 311.691.

entries.reviewSummary: Tied-house financial interest prohibitions, misdemeanor penalties, marketing/equipment definitions, 20 permitted supplier-retailer activities, nonalcoholic tying ban, exclusive-dealing ban, charitable contributions, and tourism retail exceptions.

headings.title: Tied-house prohibition and tourism distiller retail license
headings.reviewNote: Bars distillers, wholesalers, winemakers, and brewers from retail financial interests or furnishing equipment/credit (except ordinary commercial credit), while permitting Missouri distillers to hold a nearby by-the-drink retail license for tourism.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties for tied-house violations
headings.reviewNote: Makes violations of subsection 1 a misdemeanor punishable by a $1,000 fine (first offense), $5,000 fine (second), and $10,000 fine or license revocation (third or subsequent).

headings.title: Definitions of promotional materials and dispensing accessories
headings.reviewNote: Defines seven terms: consumer advertising specialties, equipment and supplies, nonrefrigeration dispensing accessories, permanent and temporary point-of-sale advertising materials, product display, and promotion.

headings.title: Permitted supplier and wholesaler activities with retailers
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates twenty permitted activities with retail licensees, including capped displays ($300), permanent POS ($500/yr), temporary permit gifts, cost sales of equipment, beer dispensing accessories, cleaning, 750 mL samples, combo packs, multi-retailer ads (note 2020 8th Cir. First Amendment ruling in source notes), sweepstakes, stocking, outside signs, and quality withdrawals; excludes consignment sales.

headings.title: Nonalcoholic beverage tying ban and fixture restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Bars dual alcoholic/nonalcoholic producers or vendors from tying or combining sales (except sub. 4(8)) and prohibits using nonalcoholic fixtures or equipment for regulated alcoholic products.

headings.title: Exclusive-dealing and exclusionary purchase agreements prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits distillers, wholesalers, brewers, and winemakers from requiring retailers by agreement or otherwise to purchase intoxicating liquor to the exclusion of competitors.

headings.title: Nonrefrigeration dispensing accessories for spirits and wine
headings.reviewNote: Permits distillers, winemakers, or wholesalers to lend, give, rent, sell, install, or repair nonrefrigeration dispensing accessories for premixed distilled spirits and wine, requiring one-year recordkeeping.

headings.title: Contributions to licensed charitable and educational organizations
headings.reviewNote: Permits distillers, wholesalers, winemakers, and brewers to contribute money or merchandise to licensed charitable, fraternal, civic, service, veterans', religious (section 313.005), or educational organizations if unrelated to retail operations.

headings.title: Advertising payments in tax-exempt organization programs
headings.reviewNote: Permits distillers, brewers, wholesalers, and winemakers to pay for advertisements in programs or brochures of tax-exempt organizations licensed under section 311.090 at the same rate paid by other vendors.

headings.title: Brewer financial interest in owned entertainment facilities
headings.reviewNote: Permits a brewer or manufacturer (and its officers, employees, or agents) to hold a retail liquor financial interest at entertainment facilities such as arenas and stadiums owned in whole or part by the brewer or its affiliates.

headings.title: Tourism retail drink license near Missouri winery
headings.reviewNote: Permits an in-state wine manufacturer to apply for a retail by-the-drink license for premises in close proximity to the winery, subject to section 311.290 hours and Sunday 6:00 a.m. to Monday 1:30 a.m. hours.

headings.title: Tourism retail drink license for Missouri wines
headings.reviewNote: Permits a tourism retail by-the-drink license where at least 75% of intoxicating liquor sold consists of Missouri-produced wines from section 311.190 manufacturers, open Mon–Sat 6:00 a.m. to midnight and Sun 6:00 a.m. to Mon 1:30 a.m.

entries.reviewSummary: Monetary contributions by alcohol licensees to registered not-for-profit organizations for special event and festival infrastructure expenses unrelated to alcohol sales, plus ATC audit access.

headings.title: Monetary contributions for not-for-profit special events
headings.reviewNote: Permits distillers, wholesalers, winemakers, and brewers to contribute money for special events where alcohol is sold to a registered, non-licensed not-for-profit (<40% liquor licensees, no private inurement) strictly for infrastructure expenses unrelated to alcohol sales.

headings.title: Monetary contributions for section 316.150 festivals
headings.reviewNote: Permits distillers, wholesalers, winemakers, brewers, and retailers to contribute money for section 316.150 festivals to a registered not-for-profit with no private inurement solely for infrastructure expenses unrelated to alcohol sales.

headings.title: Division audit access to not-for-profit records
headings.reviewNote: Requires any not-for-profit organization receiving contributions under this section to allow the division of alcohol and tobacco control full access to its records for audit purposes.

entries.reviewSummary: Retailer financial interest in a distillery near an owned recreational resort, exemption from section 311.280 for resort-produced liquor, and wholesale sales without wholesaler ownership.

headings.title: Retailer financial interest in recreational resort distillery
headings.reviewNote: Permits a retailer to hold a financial interest in a distillery in close proximity to an owned recreational resort (defined as having a restaurant, at least 30 overnight rooms, and outdoor fishing or golf).

headings.title: Section 311.280 exemption for resort-manufactured liquor
headings.reviewNote: Exempts a retail by-the-drink licensee on recreational resort grounds from section 311.280 for intoxicating liquor manufactured in close proximity to the resort, while requiring section 311.280 compliance for all other liquor.

headings.title: Wholesale sales and ban on wholesaler financial interest
headings.reviewNote: Permits a recreational resort distillery licensee (source footnote notes 'licensed' in original rolls) to sell distillery-produced liquor to licensed wholesalers under sections 311.275 and 311.540, while barring any financial interest in a Missouri wholesaler.

entries.reviewSummary: 100-foot school and church liquor license prohibition with municipal consent, municipal authority to extend distance up to 300 feet, and exemptions for section 311.218, tax-exempt clubs, and pre-2004 licensed premises.

headings.title: One-hundred-foot prohibition and municipal written consent
headings.reviewNote: Bars liquor licenses within 100 feet of a school, church, or place of worship without written municipal consent after ten days' notice to nearby property owners, grandfathering licensees if a school or church opens later.

headings.title: Municipal ordinance extending prohibition up to three hundred feet
headings.reviewNote: Permits municipalities by ordinance to prohibit liquor licenses up to 300 feet from any school, church, or place of worship, grandfathering existing licensees if a school or church opens later.

headings.title: Exemptions for section 311.218 and tax-exempt organizations
headings.reviewNote: Exempts section 311.218 Fourth of July permits and licenses issued to federally tax-exempt churches, schools, and civic, service, fraternal, veteran, political, or charitable organizations from subsection 1.

headings.title: Grandfather exemption for premises licensed before 2004
headings.reviewNote: Exempts premises holding a state liquor license issued before January 1, 2004, from subsection 1 if they do not change license type, amend legal description, or go unlicensed for more than ninety days.

entries.reviewSummary: Retail off-premise keg labeling with ATC numbered tags, $50 minimum deposit and 3-month purchaser records, deposit forfeiture on missing tags, rulemaking, July 1, 2004 effective date, and local preemption.

headings.title: Definitions of keg and supervisor
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'keg' as a container holding four or more gallons of beer, wine, or intoxicating liquor designed for direct dispensing (excluding nonreturnable containers under six gallons), and defines supervisor of alcohol and tobacco control.

headings.title: ATC numbered identification tag affixed to retail kegs
headings.reviewNote: Requires each retail off-premise keg to bear a free recyclable numbered identification tag supplied by ATC and securely affixed by the licensee to the top chime handle.

headings.title: Purchaser ID, fifty-dollar deposit, and three-month records
headings.reviewNote: Requires valid ID, a minimum $50 deposit per keg, an ATC identification form recording sale and purchaser details, a signed purchaser liability acknowledgment, and retention of the form for at least three months.

headings.title: Deposit retention for missing tags and tag retention
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits refunding deposits on kegs returned without an intact legible tag, permits retaining forfeited deposits, requires recording return date and tag condition, and requires removing and retaining returned tags with the form.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for keg registration forms
headings.reviewNote: Directs the supervisor of alcohol and tobacco control to design forms and promulgate administrative rules under chapter 536.

headings.title: Effective date of keg registration provisions
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that the provisions of the keg labeling and registration statute became effective on July 1, 2004.

headings.title: State preemption of local keg regulations
headings.reviewNote: Fully preempts local ordinances regulating keg selling, labeling, or registering, and states the section imposes no new or additional civil or criminal liability on retail licensees.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 311.083 governing entertainment district special licenses, common area consumption, branded containers, hours, and municipal ordinances.

headings.title: Definitions for entertainment district special licenses
headings.reviewNote: Defines common area, entertainment district (lake and river boundary criteria), and portable bar for special district licensing.

headings.title: Special license issuance and operating hours
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the supervisor to issue entertainment district special licenses for retail drink sales, including from portable bars, until 1:30 a.m. Monday through Sunday.

headings.title: Annual special license fee
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an annual license fee of three hundred dollars for an entertainment district special license.

headings.title: Carrying and consuming drinks in common areas
headings.reviewNote: Allows patrons to carry alcoholic beverages between licensed premises and common areas within the district, prohibiting removal outside district boundaries.

headings.title: Distinctive logo container requirement
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that beverages served within the entertainment district be dispensed in containers bearing the licensee's trade name, logo, or unique mark.

headings.title: Licensee responsibility for district violations
headings.reviewNote: Places sole responsibility on the special license holder for alcohol violations occurring on its premises, portable bars, and associated common areas.

headings.title: Municipal ordinance authority and local regulations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the municipal governing body to adopt ordinances establishing district boundaries, approval procedures, and local regulations.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 311.084 establishing lake-area entertainment district special licenses, portable bar rules, common area consumption, and branded container mandates.

headings.title: Definitions for lake entertainment district special licenses
headings.reviewNote: Defines common area, lake-area entertainment district, and portable bar for special entertainment district licensing.

headings.title: Special license issuance and portable bar hours
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the supervisor to issue special licenses to sell liquor from portable bars within the district from 6:00 a.m. to 3:00 a.m. Monday through Saturday and until 1:30 a.m. Sunday.

headings.title: Annual entertainment district special license fee
headings.reviewNote: Sets an annual fee of three hundred dollars for an entertainment district special license under this section.

headings.title: Common area consumption and minor identification procedures
headings.reviewNote: Allows patrons to consume drinks in common areas, prohibits taking drinks outside boundaries, and requires age-distinguishing measures for minors.

headings.title: Unique branded container requirement for licensees
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensees to serve alcoholic beverages in containers displaying the licensee's trade name, logo, or unique mark.

headings.title: Licensee responsibility for alcohol violations in district
headings.reviewNote: Holds the special license holder solely responsible for alcohol violations occurring at its portable bars and common areas.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 311.086 governing Kansas City downtown entertainment district licenses, portable bars, pedestrian common areas, and branded cup rules.

headings.title: Definitions for Kansas City entertainment district
headings.reviewNote: Defines common area, central business entertainment district (Kansas City), and portable bar for special district licensing.

headings.title: Special license issuance and extended closing hours
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes issuance of an entertainment district special license for portable bars to sell liquor until 3:00 a.m. Monday through Saturday and until 1:30 a.m. on Sunday.

headings.title: Annual special permit fee
headings.reviewNote: Imposes an annual permit fee of three hundred dollars for a Kansas City entertainment district special license.

headings.title: Common area consumption and district boundary limits
headings.reviewNote: Allows patrons to carry drinks between licensed premises and common areas closed to traffic, prohibiting taking alcohol outside the district.

headings.title: Mandatory distinctive branded containers
headings.reviewNote: Requires beverages in the entertainment district to be served in containers bearing the licensee's logo, trade name, or unique mark.

headings.title: Licensee liability for common area violations
headings.reviewNote: Holds the special licensee solely responsible for alcohol violations occurring at its portable bars and within common areas.

entries.reviewSummary: Municipal retail liquor-by-the-drink licensing with voter-approval thresholds for cities under 19,500 and tax-exempt organization exceptions, plus multi-building premises validity for qualifying organizations.

headings.title: Liquor-by-the-drink licensing in cities and requirements
headings.reviewNote: Permits retail liquor-by-the-drink licensing in incorporated cities, requiring voter approval in cities under 19,500 (except malt liquor, light wine <=14%, and specified 501(c)/(d) tax-exempt organizations) and restricting non-city licenses to those exceptions.

headings.title: Multi-building validity for tax-exempt organization permits
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a section 311.090 license held by a charitable, fraternal, religious, service, or veterans' organization whose premises include two or more buildings in close proximity is valid at any such building.

entries.reviewSummary: Retail liquor-by-the-drink licenses for USCG-licensed passenger boats carrying 30 or more passengers on navigable waters and the $300 annual license fee.

headings.title: Passenger boat and vessel liquor-by-the-drink license
headings.reviewNote: Permits licensing retail liquor-by-the-drink sales on USCG-licensed vessels carrying 30 or more passengers for hire moored in or within 200 yards of a licensable Missouri location, valid while underway (source note: 2016 S.B. 994 veto override effective 10-14-16).

headings.title: Three-hundred-dollar annual vessel license fee
headings.reviewNote: Requires holders of a boat or vessel retail liquor-by-the-drink license under this section to pay $300 per year to the director of revenue.

entries.reviewSummary: Resort and restaurant retail drink licensing, seasonal resort restaurant definitions and prorated temporary licenses, applicable operating laws, and 90-day temporary licenses for new resorts or restaurants.

headings.title: Resort liquor-by-the-drink license and resort definition
headings.reviewNote: Permits retail drink licenses for resorts, defined as >=30-room hotels with a 60%-food restaurant, restaurants with >=$75,000 gross receipts (>=$50,000 nonalcoholic), or seasonal resort restaurants, covering all resort-owned facilities.

headings.title: Seasonal resort restaurants and temporary licenses
headings.reviewNote: Defines seasonal resort restaurants (open <=8 consecutive months, 50% prepared meals), authorizes 90-day temporary licenses for new ones (<12 weeks) with prorated fees, and clarifies returning seasonal restaurants are not new.

headings.title: Application of hours, county fees, and retail laws
headings.reviewNote: Applies section 311.290 hours, section 311.220 county fees, and all other retail liquor-by-the-drink laws to resorts in the same manner as section 311.090 establishments.

headings.title: Ninety-day temporary license for new resorts or restaurants
headings.reviewNote: Permits issuing a prorated 90-day temporary drink license to a new resort or restaurant (<90 days in operation) projecting at least $75,000 annual gross receipts with at least $50,000 from nonalcoholic sales.

entries.reviewSummary: Definition of common eating and drinking area, $300 annual off-premises common-area drink licenses, $200 Sunday licenses, and $300 convention trade area 3:00 a.m. extended-hours permits.

headings.title: Definition of common eating and drinking area
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'common eating and drinking area' as a shared area within a building or group of buildings maintained by shared charges with at least $275,000 in annual or projected prepared-food gross income for tenants lacking internal seating.

headings.title: Common eating and drinking area drink license and fee
headings.reviewNote: Permits licensing retail drink sales for consumption in a common eating and drinking area for $300 per year, applying section 311.290 hours, section 311.220 local fees, and general retail drink laws.

headings.title: Sunday common eating and drinking area license
headings.reviewNote: Permits issuing a Sunday license (6:00 a.m. Sunday to 1:30 a.m. Monday) for retail drink sales consumed in a common eating and drinking area for an additional $200 annual fee.

headings.title: Extended-hours convention trade area permit
headings.reviewNote: Permits common-area licensees in a designated convention trade area to obtain a special permit to remain open 1:30 a.m. to 3:00 a.m. all days of the week for an additional $300 annual fee.

entries.reviewSummary: Controlled access liquor cabinet systems for qualified hotels, operating conditions and employee rules, 90-day temporary licenses for new establishments, and wholesaler sales of qualified containers.

headings.title: Definitions for hotel controlled access liquor cabinets
headings.reviewNote: Defines controlled access liquor cabinet, cabinet system, qualified establishment (>=40 rooms, >=60% food, >=$100,000 annual/projected food sales), qualified packages (50–200 mL spirits/wine, any size beer/malt liquor), registered guest, and room.

headings.title: Controlled access cabinet license and operating conditions
headings.reviewNote: Directs issuance of cabinet system licenses to qualified drink licensees subject to six conditions: adult registered guest access, age verification, >=18 employees with local permits, restocking hours, removal on request, and guest billing.

headings.title: Temporary ninety-day license for new qualified establishments
headings.reviewNote: Permits issuing a 90-day temporary controlled access liquor cabinet license to a new qualified establishment (<90 days in operation) projecting annual prepared-food sales exceeding $100,000.

headings.title: Wholesaler sales of qualified cabinet containers
headings.reviewNote: Permits licensed wholesalers to sell qualified package sizes to qualified establishments for cabinet systems, restricting any specially authorized sizes solely to sales via the cabinet system.

entries.reviewSummary: Carryout and open-container-exempt vehicle transportation of resealed unfinished wine bottles from restaurant bars and wineries, plus statutory definition of winery.

headings.title: Carryout of unfinished wine from restaurant bars
headings.reviewNote: Permits restaurant bars (referencing repealed section 311.097 per source footnote) to let patrons carry out unfinished wine if a meal was ordered, wine was partially consumed, a dated receipt is provided, and bottles are resealed in tamperproof transparent bags.

headings.title: Vehicle transportation of restaurant unfinished wine
headings.reviewNote: Exempts transporting unfinished restaurant-bar wine in a vehicle from state and local open-container laws while the person possesses the dated receipt and intact tamperproof transparent bag seals.

headings.title: Carryout of unfinished wine from wineries
headings.reviewNote: Permits wineries to let patrons carry out unfinished wine if partially consumed at the winery, accompanied by a dated receipt, and resealed in one-time-use tamperproof transparent bags.

headings.title: Vehicle transportation of winery unfinished wine
headings.reviewNote: Exempts transporting unfinished winery wine from state and local open-container laws while the person possesses the dated winery receipt and intact tamperproof transparent bag seals.

headings.title: Definition of winery
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'winery' for purposes of this section as any establishment at which wine is made.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.174 authorizing 3:00 a.m. extended liquor sales in Kansas City convention trade areas, annual fees, and local ordinance adoption.

headings.title: Extended closing hours in convention trade area
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes retail drink licensees in Kansas City and Jackson County convention trade areas to obtain a special permit to remain open until 3:00 a.m. daily.

headings.title: Additional annual convention area permit fee
headings.reviewNote: Imposes an additional annual permit fee of three hundred dollars for the extended-hours convention trade area permit.

headings.title: Municipal ordinance approval requirement in charter county
headings.reviewNote: Provides that extended hours do not take effect in incorporated areas of charter counties until adopted by local municipal ordinance.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.176 authorizing 3:00 a.m. extended liquor sales in St. Louis City convention trade areas for qualifying businesses and resorts.

headings.title: Extended closing hours in St. Louis convention area
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes retail drink licensees in St. Louis City convention trade areas meeting $150,000 annual sales or resort criteria to remain open until 3:00 a.m.

headings.title: Additional annual convention area permit fee
headings.reviewNote: Requires payment of an additional annual fee of three hundred dollars for the St. Louis convention trade area extended-hours permit.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 311.178 governing 3:00 a.m. liquor sales in St. Louis County convention areas and lake resort overnight-guest permits.

headings.title: Extended hours in St. Louis County convention area
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes retail drink licensees in St. Louis County convention trade areas meeting $150,000 annual sales or resort criteria to remain open until 3:00 a.m.

headings.title: Special extended hours permit for lake resorts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes qualified resorts in designated lake counties to obtain special permits for 3:00 a.m. closing under an approved overnight-guest service plan.

headings.title: Restriction of late sales to overnight guests
headings.reviewNote: Makes it unlawful for lake resort special permittees to sell liquor between 1:30 a.m. and 3:00 a.m. to anyone other than registered overnight guests.

headings.title: Additional annual resort permit fee
headings.reviewNote: Imposes an additional annual permit fee of three hundred dollars for the extended hours permit under this section.

headings.title: Municipal ordinance requirement in charter county
headings.reviewNote: Provides that extended hours do not apply in incorporated areas of charter counties until adopted by municipal ordinance.

entries.reviewSummary: Special permits for St. Louis Lambert and Kansas City International Airports allowing 4:00 a.m. opening, designated-area carryout, branded containers, and $300 annual fee.

headings.title: International airport 4:00 a.m. permit and carryout rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits St. Louis Lambert and Kansas City International Airport drink licensees to obtain a special permit to open at 4:00 a.m. (including Sundays), allow drinks in designated airport areas (not airplanes), and require unique licensee-branded containers.

headings.title: Additional annual international airport permit fee
headings.reviewNote: Imposes an additional annual permit fee of three hundred dollars for the extended-hours airport permit.

entries.reviewSummary: Manufacturer, wholesaler, and solicitor licensing with ten annual fee tiers, merchant's license exemption, malt liquor territory limits, and wholesaler sales to gaming commission licensees.

headings.title: Manufacturer, wholesaler, and solicitor licenses and fees
headings.reviewNote: Requires state licenses to manufacture, distill, blend, sell, or solicit intoxicating liquor and sets ten annual fee tiers ($50 to $500) by alcohol content, wholesale/solicitor privilege, and vintage wine.

headings.title: Merchant's license exemption for solicitors and manufacturers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts solicitors, manufacturers, and blenders of intoxicating liquor from needing a merchant's license for sales at the place of manufacture or in quantities of at least one gallon.

headings.title: Malt liquor privileges subject to territorial statutes
headings.reviewNote: Subjects the section's malt liquor selling privileges to the geographical area limitations and exclusive territory provisions of sections 311.181 and 311.182.

headings.title: Wholesaler sales to gaming commission licensees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes wholesalers licensed to sell to retail dealers to sell intoxicating liquor to licensees licensed by the Missouri Gaming Commission under section 313.840.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandatory brewer-wholesaler geographic territory agreements for malt liquor, written territory modification and service verification, ban on resale price maintenance, and section 311.720 exclusion.

headings.title: Geographic territory agreements and emergency servicing exception
headings.reviewNote: Requires malt liquor wholesalers to file sworn territory statements and written brewer agreements, bars sales outside designated areas, and allows temporary servicing by another wholesaler during fire, flood, or similar emergencies with consent and approval.

headings.title: Written agreement and service verification for territory changes
headings.reviewNote: Permits changing a designated geographic area only by written brewer-wholesaler agreement filed with the supervisor, who shall require verification that service levels will not be affected.

headings.title: Prohibition on resale price maintenance in agreements
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any provision of a required written territorial agreement from expressly, impliedly, or operationally establishing or maintaining beer resale prices.

headings.title: Inapplicability of section 311.720
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the provisions of section 311.720 shall not apply to this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibition on dual malt liquor wholesalers in a designated geographic area, tiered misdemeanor fines for territorial violations, and inapplicability of section 311.720.

headings.title: Exclusive single wholesaler per designated geographic area
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a brewer or manufacturer from contracting to establish an additional wholesaler for the same malt liquor brands in a designated area, while preserving enforcement of written section 311.181 agreements.

headings.title: Misdemeanor fines for geographic territory violations
headings.reviewNote: Makes violations of section 311.181 or this section by a wholesaler or brewer a misdemeanor punishable exclusively by fines of $1,000 (first offense), $5,000 (second), and $25,000 (third).

headings.title: Inapplicability of section 311.720
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the provisions of section 311.720 shall not apply to this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Wine direct shipper licensing, ten shipper compliance obligations, annual renewal, alcohol carrier licensing and delivery duties, and chapter 536 rulemaking with nonseverability.

headings.title: Wine direct shipper license and application requirements
headings.reviewNote: Permits licensed in-state or out-of-state wine manufacturers to obtain a wine direct shipper license to ship up to two cases per month to 21+ Missouri residents upon submitting an application, state license, and federal TTB winery license.

headings.title: Compliance obligations of wine direct shipper licensees
headings.reviewNote: Sets ten duties for direct shippers: 2-case monthly cap, licensed carriers only, TTB registration, on-premises manufacture, conspicuous 21+ label, annual Jan. 31 out-of-state report and excise tax, in-state reporting, audits, and Missouri jurisdiction consent.

headings.title: Annual renewal of wine direct shipper license
headings.reviewNote: Permits a wine direct shipper licensee to annually renew its license with ATC by submitting all items required in subsection 1.

headings.title: Alcohol carrier license for direct wine delivery
headings.reviewNote: Permits carriers to obtain an alcohol carrier license from ATC authorizing transportation and delivery of wine shipments directly to Missouri residents aged 21 or older.

headings.title: Delivery restrictions and recordkeeping for alcohol carriers
headings.reviewNote: Requires alcohol carrier licensees to avoid delivery to minors or intoxicated persons, require valid ID/age proof, obtain an adult signature, and maintain shipment and signature records.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Permits ATC to promulgate implementing rules subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028, with a nonseverability clause voiding post-August 28, 2007 rulemaking authority and rules if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Domestic wine and brandy manufacturer licensing ($5 per 500 gallons up to $300), 15% out-of-state material allowance, natural disaster crop-loss exception, and wholesale/winery retail sales.

headings.title: Domestic wine and brandy manufacturer license fee
headings.reviewNote: Sets a license fee (in lieu of section 311.180) of $5 per 500 gallons up to $300 for manufacturing up to 500,000 gallons of Missouri-grown wine (<=18% alcohol) or brandy (<=34% alcohol).

headings.title: Fifteen-percent out-of-state material allowance
headings.reviewNote: Permits a licensed manufacturer to use out-of-state wine- and brandy-making materials in any calendar year up to 15% of the wine entered into fermentation in the prior calendar year.

headings.title: Natural disaster crop-loss out-of-state purchase exception
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director of agriculture in a natural disaster crop-loss year to determine the percentage of loss and allow Missouri wineries to purchase an additional percentage of out-of-state produce.

headings.title: Bulk, wholesale, winery retail, and on-premises sales
headings.reviewNote: Permits licensed manufacturers to trade bulk/packaged products with other licensed manufacturers, sell to wineries/wholesalers/retailers except Sundays, and offer winery samples, original-package sales, and on-premises consumption (Mon–Sat 6 a.m.–midnight, Sun 6 a.m.–Mon 1:30 a.m.).

entries.reviewSummary: Vintage wine definition, private collection consignment auctions, chapter 343 auctioneer licensing and disqualifications, premises/six-auction limits ($500 fee), shipping, tastings, and misdemeanor labeling penalty.

headings.title: Definition of vintage wine
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'vintage wine' as bottled domestic white, rose, or sparkling wine >=5 years old, domestic red wine >=10 years old, or imported white, rose, red, sparkling, or port wine >=3 years old.

headings.title: Consignment auction sales and private-collection labeling
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes municipalities and private owners (including fiduciaries and court officers) to sell private vintage wine collections on consignment through a licensed auctioneer, who shall affix a permanent private-collection label.

headings.title: Vintage wine auctioneer license qualifications and disqualifications
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes issuing vintage wine auction licenses to chapter 343 auctioneers at fixed locations in charter first-class county cities, disqualifying felons, ch. 311 violators, current/revoked liquor licensees, and auctioneers with under 10 years' continuous in-state business.

headings.title: Premises restriction, six-auction annual cap, and fee
headings.reviewNote: Restricts auctions to the auctioneer's business premises, prohibits on-premises consumption or opening (except as provided), limits the one-year license to six auctions per year, and sets a $500 annual fee.

headings.title: Shipping and storage rules for vintage wine
headings.reviewNote: Regulates the shipment, warehousing, and transportation of vintage wine within Missouri.

headings.title: Pre-sale wine tastings within twenty-four hours
headings.reviewNote: Permits conducting wine tastings on premises within twenty-four hours prior to a scheduled vintage wine auction.

headings.title: Application of general liquor control statutes
headings.reviewNote: Subjects vintage wine licensees to general liquor control provisions governing storage, acquisition, and sale.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for fraudulent vintage labeling
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowingly affixing a false vintage wine label or misrepresenting wine origin as a class C misdemeanor with license revocation.

entries.reviewSummary: Vintage wine definition, municipal sealed-bid sales and labeling, designated employee licensing and disqualifications, local ordinance compliance, six-sale cap ($50 fee), shipping, tastings, and penalties.

headings.title: Definition of vintage wine
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'vintage wine' as bottled domestic white, rose, or sparkling wine >=5 years old, domestic red wine >=10 years old, or imported white, rose, red, sparkling, or port wine >=3 years old.

headings.title: Municipal sealed-bid sales and private-collection labeling
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes municipalities owning private vintage wine collections to sell them by sealed bid (with optional minimum bid and rejection rights) through a designated municipal employee who affixes a permanent private-collection label.

headings.title: Designated municipal employee license and disqualifications
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the supervisor to license a designated municipal employee for sealed-bid vintage wine sales, disqualifying persons with felony or ch. 311 convictions or current/revoked wholesale or retail liquor licenses.

headings.title: Cumulative with county and municipal license requirements
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the state sealed-bid vintage wine license is in addition to any county or municipal ordinance license or permit requirements.

headings.title: Premises consumption ban, six-sale limit, and fifty-dollar fee
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits on-premises consumption or opening on municipal premises (except tastings), sets a one-year license term allowing up to six sales per year, and sets a $50 annual fee paid by the municipality.

headings.title: Warehousing, shipping, and tax payment obligations
headings.reviewNote: Governs municipal storage, warehousing, delivery, and payment of applicable state and local sales taxes on vintage wine sales.

headings.title: Pre-bid tastings on municipal storage premises
headings.reviewNote: Permits holding vintage wine tastings on the storage premises within twenty-four hours before sealed bids are accepted.

headings.title: Compliance with general off-premises liquor laws
headings.reviewNote: Subjects the designated municipal employee to all general off-premises liquor control statutes not inconsistent with this section.

headings.title: Penalties for failure of reasonable diligence
headings.reviewNote: Imposes class C misdemeanor penalties and license cancellation if a designated employee affixes labels without reasonable diligence as to bona fide private collection origin.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 311.195 defining microbreweries, barrel fees, retail drink licensing, wholesale sales, and self-distribution exemptions.

headings.title: Definition of microbrewery and barrel capacity
headings.reviewNote: Defines microbrewery as a business whose primary activity is brewing and selling beer with annual production of 10,000 barrels or less.

headings.title: Microbrewery license fee schedule
headings.reviewNote: Establishes microbrewery license fees at five dollars per one hundred barrels up to a maximum fee of two hundred fifty dollars.

headings.title: Retail drink license on microbrewery premises
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes microbreweries to obtain retail licenses to sell intoxicating liquor by the drink on premises or nearby, limiting microbrewers to ten retail licenses.

headings.title: Sale to wholesalers and tied-house prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Permits microbrewers to sell beer produced on premises to licensed wholesalers while prohibiting financial interests in wholesaler businesses.

headings.title: Exemption from wholesale purchase requirements for self-brewed beer
headings.reviewNote: Exempts microbrewers holding retail drink licenses from section 311.280 wholesale purchasing requirements for beer produced on premises.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.197 establishing standards for wholesalers furnishing malt liquor samples to retailers and brand differentiation criteria.

headings.title: Wholesaler furnishing of malt liquor samples
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes malt liquor wholesalers to furnish samples up to seventy-two fluid ounces to retailers who have not previously purchased the brand, requiring recordkeeping.

headings.title: Brand differentiation standards for samples
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that brands are differentiated by product name, class, type, or kind, rather than packaging, style, or label design.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 311.198 governing brewer and wholesaler leasing of portable refrigeration units to retailers, 5-year caps, rules, and 2026 sunset.

headings.title: Lease of portable refrigeration units to retailers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes brewers to lease portable refrigeration units up to forty cubic feet to retailers or wholesalers at cost plus two percent, with advertising and reporting rules.

headings.title: Five-year maximum duration for refrigeration leases
headings.reviewNote: Restricts refrigeration unit leases and subleases to a maximum of five years and prohibits automatic renewal clauses.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking authority for unit leases
headings.reviewNote: Grants rulemaking authority to the division under chapter 536 and includes nonseverability provisions.

headings.title: Expiration date for refrigeration unit leasing
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section expires on January 1, 2026 (source note records 'Expires 1-01-26'), while leases or subleases executed prior to January 1, 2026 remain in effect until their expiration.

entries.reviewSummary: Retail liquor license categories and annual fees for original package liquor, original package and by-the-drink malt liquor (with Sunday hours), malt liquor/light wine, all-liquor by the drink, railroad cars, and application forms.

headings.title: Original package retail liquor license and hundred-dollar fee
headings.reviewNote: Restricts original-package intoxicating liquor licenses to six enumerated store types maintaining at least $1,000 in invoice stock, prohibits on-premises consumption or opening, and sets a $100 annual fee.

headings.title: Original package malt liquor permit and Sunday hours
headings.reviewNote: Sets a $50 annual permit fee for retail original-package malt liquor sales, defines 'original package' (one or more standard bottles, cans, or pouches), and allows sales from 6:00 a.m. Sunday to 1:30 a.m. Monday.

headings.title: Malt liquor by-the-drink license and Sunday hours
headings.reviewNote: Sets a $50 annual license fee for retail malt liquor by-the-drink sales for on-premises consumption and allows sales from 6:00 a.m. Sunday to 1:30 a.m. Monday.

headings.title: Malt liquor and light wine by-the-drink license
headings.reviewNote: Sets a $50 annual license fee for retail by-the-drink sales of malt liquor and light wines containing not more than 14% alcohol by weight made from grapes, berries, fruits, and vegetables.

headings.title: All-kinds intoxicating liquor by-the-drink license
headings.reviewNote: Sets a $300 annual license fee for retail by-the-drink sales of all kinds of intoxicating liquor for on-premises consumption, which includes original-package sales.

headings.title: Railroad and sleeping car company liquor license
headings.reviewNote: Sets a $100 annual license fee for railroad and railway sleeping car companies to sell all kinds of intoxicating liquor on dining, buffet, and observation cars, plus $1 per posted duplicate car license.

headings.title: Supervisor application forms and fee prepayment requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires all license applications to be made on forms prescribed by the supervisor of alcohol and tobacco control and bars license issuance until the prescribed fee is paid to the director of revenue.

entries.reviewSummary: Retail off-premises sales of 32-to-128-ounce draft beer growlers by employees aged 21+, ban on supplier-furnished equipment/containers, mandatory labels and federal health warnings, and sanitary on-demand filling procedures.

headings.title: Retail sale of draft beer in growlers
headings.reviewNote: Permits section 311.200(1) original-package retail licensees to sell 32 to 128 fluid ounces of draft beer for off-premises consumption in containers filled on premises by employees aged 21 or older.

headings.title: Prohibition on supplier-furnished equipment or containers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits interpreting any law or ATC rule to allow wholesalers, distributors, or manufacturers to furnish dispensing/cooling equipment or growler containers to section 311.200(1) retailers.

headings.title: Required container labels and federal health warning
headings.reviewNote: Requires a label or tag (>=3 mm type, <=12 chars/in) listing seven product/filler items including an unfiltered/refrigeration notice, plus the federal health warning statement under 27 CFR Sections 16.20 to 16.22.

headings.title: On-demand employee filling, sanitation, and sealing procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires on-demand filling (no prefilling) solely by retailer employees using either bottom-to-top food-grade sanitized tubes or an FDA Food Code 2009 Section 3-304.17(c) contamination-free process, followed by sealing.

entries.reviewSummary: Retailer-packaged to-go alcoholic beverages with on-premises meals (<=128 oz, 2-to-1 meal ratio, tamperproof seal), mandatory alcohol labels, FDA Food Code sanitation, and ban on supplier-furnished containers.

headings.title: Retail to-go alcohol sales with food purchase
headings.reviewNote: Permits on-premises retail drink licensees (via employees aged 21+) to sell to-go beverages meeting six conditions: rigid leakproof sealable container (no straw holes), <=128 oz, simultaneous on-premises meal, max 2x meal servings, dated receipt/record, and tamperproof bag or tape.

headings.title: Mandatory business and alcohol content container label
headings.reviewNote: Requires affixing a label or tag (>=3 mm type, <=12 chars/in) containing the filling business's name and address and stating 'THIS BEVERAGE CONTAINS ALCOHOL.'

headings.title: Compliance with 2009 FDA Food Code
headings.reviewNote: Requires container filling under this section to comply with Section 3-304.17(C) of the 2009 Food and Drug Administration Food Code.

headings.title: Prohibition on supplier-furnished to-go containers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits interpreting any law or ATC rule to allow wholesalers, distributors, or manufacturers to furnish containers filled under subsection 1 to retail licensees.

entries.reviewSummary: Statewide 2026 FIFA World Cup temporary extension of retail drink hours (6:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m., June 11–July 19, 2026), no special permit required, local opt-out/modification ordinances, and July 20, 2026 expiration.

headings.title: Definition of FIFA World Cup Tournament
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'FIFA World Cup Tournament' as the quadrennial international soccer tournament organized by the Federation Internationale de Football Association.

headings.title: Temporary statewide extended hours during 2026 tournament
headings.reviewNote: Permits retail by-the-drink licensees statewide, from June 11 through July 19, 2026, to operate 24 hours a day and sell, serve, and allow consumption between 6:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. the following day.

headings.title: No special permit or commission application required
headings.reviewNote: Provides that licensees need not apply to the commission or obtain a special temporary license or permit for the temporary extension, subject to local restrictions under subsection 4 or other local laws.

headings.title: Local political subdivision opt-out or hour modification
headings.reviewNote: Permits any objecting city, county, district, or political subdivision by ordinance to exempt itself from the section or modify temporary hours between ordinary permissible hours and the section's maximum.

headings.title: Expiration on July 20, 2026
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section expires on July 20, 2026 (source note records 'Expires 7-20-26').

entries.reviewSummary: Retailer-monitored customer self-dispensing systems for beer (up to 32 oz) and wine (up to 16 oz) per employee authorization, and ban on supplier-furnished self-dispensing equipment or maintenance.

headings.title: Self-dispensing beer and wine system authorization
headings.reviewNote: Permits retail by-the-drink licensees to use a licensee-monitored self-dispensing system for beer or wine after employee authorization of up to 32 ounces of beer or 16 ounces of wine per patron per authorization (source note: 2016 S.B. 994 veto override eff. 10-14-16).

headings.title: Prohibition on supplier-furnished equipment or maintenance
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits interpreting any law or rule to allow wholesalers, distributors, or manufacturers to furnish self-dispensing or cooling equipment or provide maintenance, sanitation, or repair services.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.210 establishing license application procedures, director of revenue remittances, and supervisor investigatory powers.

headings.title: License application and fee remittance procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires all liquor license applications to be made to the supervisor of liquor control, with fees remitted to the director of revenue.

headings.title: Supervisor authority to grant or deny licenses
headings.reviewNote: Empowers and requires the supervisor to approve or disapprove license applications, send written grounds and return remittances upon disapproval, and file issuance notices and remittances with the director of revenue for duplicate receipts upon approval.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.218 authorizing temporary Fourth of July celebration permits for civic groups to sell wine and malt liquor, and defining wine.

headings.title: Temporary Fourth of July liquor permit
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes temporary permits for civic and charitable organizations to sell wine and malt liquor for up to seven days during Fourth of July events for a $100 fee.

headings.title: Definition of wine for temporary celebration
headings.reviewNote: Defines wine for temporary Fourth of July celebration permits as a beverage containing not more than fourteen percent alcohol by weight.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.220 governing county and municipal liquor license fee ceilings, local regulatory ordinances, and license display mandates.

headings.title: County and municipal liquor license fees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes counties to charge liquor license fees up to 100% and municipalities up to 150% of the corresponding state liquor license fee.

headings.title: Municipal regulatory ordinance authority and penalties
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes city councils and aldermen to enact and enforce liquor regulation ordinances and penalize local violations consistent with state law.

headings.title: Prominent display and filing of local licenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensees to prominently display city or county licenses on premises and file a copy with the state supervisor within ten days of issuance.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 311.240 establishing June 30 license expiration, federal tax receipts, premises descriptions, May 1 renewals, and late charges.

headings.title: Annual license term and prorated license tax
headings.reviewNote: Provides that state liquor licenses expire on June 30th and requires applicants to pay prorated monthly twelfths for the remaining term.

headings.title: Federal tax stamp or receipt requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensees to affix an official federal excise or occupational tax stamp or receipt to the license and file a copy within ten days.

headings.title: Premises description and location restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that every liquor license particularly describe the licensed premises, prohibiting sales at any other location.

headings.title: Annual license renewal application deadline
headings.reviewNote: Requires license renewal applications to be filed on or before May first of each calendar year.

headings.title: Tiered late charges for delinquent renewals
headings.reviewNote: Establishes progressive late renewal charges ($100 in May, $200 in June, $300 after June) for failure to meet the May first filing deadline.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.250 governing the general prohibition against license transfers, spousal death transfers, and partner withdrawals.

headings.title: Transfer to surviving spouse upon licensee death
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits license transfers generally, but authorizes transferring a deceased licensee's license to a qualified surviving spouse or next of kin.

headings.title: Continuation of business upon partner withdrawal
headings.reviewNote: Requires the supervisor, upon request when one or more partners withdraw, to permit the originally licensed remaining partner(s) to continue operating for the paid license period without a new license.

entries.reviewSummary: Five-license cap on retail by-the-drink establishments and statutory exclusions for 50%-food restaurants, $200,000-food establishments, $100,000+ live entertainment venues, and 40+-room hotels.

headings.title: Five-license limit on retail drink establishments
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any person or corporate affiliate from holding more than five retail drink licenses or selling liquor by the drink at more than five locations.

headings.title: Exemptions for restaurants, entertainment venues, and hotels
headings.reviewNote: Excludes from the five-license cap: restaurants deriving >=50% gross income from on-premises prepared food, establishments with >=$200,000 annual on-premises food income, live entertainment facilities with >$100,000 annual admission receipts, and >=40-room overnight lodging establishments.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.270 prohibiting malt-only licensees from possessing spirits, federal spirits tax stamps, and establishing license revocation and criminal penalties.

headings.title: Unlawful possession of non-malt liquor on premises
headings.reviewNote: Makes it a misdemeanor for a malt-only retail licensee to possess, sell, or allow others to consume non-malt liquor on the licensed premises, triggering automatic revocation.

headings.title: Federal tax stamp for spirits as violation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits issuing malt liquor licenses to holders of federal spirits tax stamps, mandates revocation for possessing such stamps, and establishes prima facie proof.

headings.title: Criminal penalties for possessing federal spirits stamp
headings.reviewNote: Imposes county jail imprisonment of three months to one year and fines up to $1,000 for possessing a federal spirits stamp while holding a malt-only license.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 311.275 establishing primary American source of supply registration requirements, definitions, vintage wine rules, and 5-day review deadlines.

headings.title: Registration as primary American source of supply
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits out-of-state solicitors from filling wholesale liquor orders in Missouri without annual registration with the division as the primary American source of supply.

headings.title: Wholesaler restriction to registered primary sources
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits licensed wholesalers from ordering or receiving intoxicating liquor from solicitors not registered as the primary American source of supply.

headings.title: Definition of primary American source of supply
headings.reviewNote: Defines primary American source of supply as the distiller, producer, owner, bottler, or exclusive agent closest to the manufacturer in commerce.

headings.title: Vintage wine solicitor primary source registration
headings.reviewNote: Permits vintage wine solicitors to register as the primary American source of supply if approved by federal TTB and not previously registered.

headings.title: Five-day application processing and conditional approval
headings.reviewNote: Requires the supervisor to approve or deny primary source applications within five working days, providing for conditional approval upon delay and prioritizing in-state applicants.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.280 mandating retailer purchases from licensed Missouri wholesalers and prohibiting the sale of mutilated cartons or misleadingly repackaged products.

headings.title: Retailers restricted to licensed Missouri wholesalers
headings.reviewNote: Requires retail liquor licensees to purchase intoxicating liquor solely from licensed Missouri wholesalers, making unauthorized purchases a misdemeanor.

headings.title: Prohibition on selling mutilated packages or repackaging
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits retailers from selling malt liquor in mutilated or cut-apart wholesale cartons or repackaging containers in a misleading manner obscuring labels.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.293 governing Sunday retail package and drink sales hours, state and local permit fees, and convention area exceptions.

headings.title: Sunday retail sales license and state fee
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes retail liquor licensees to obtain a special license to sell liquor between 6:00 a.m. on Sunday and 1:30 a.m. on Monday for a $200 annual fee.

headings.title: Local municipal and county Sunday license fees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes cities and counties to collect an additional local license fee up to three hundred dollars for Sunday retail liquor sales.

headings.title: Closing time exemptions for convention trade areas
headings.reviewNote: Provides that Sunday closing hour restrictions do not apply to permittees operating under extended convention trade area permits.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.294 authorizing retail package liquor stores to conduct product tastings under a $25 permit while barring on-premises sales.

headings.title: Tasting permit for retail package liquor licensees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes retail package liquor licensees to obtain a special annual permit for twenty-five dollars to conduct wine, malt beverage, and distilled spirit tastings.

headings.title: Prohibition on sales for on-premises consumption
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that tasting permits do not authorize the licensee to sell wine, malt beverages, or spirits for consumption on premises.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.297 governing alcohol tasting samples off and on retail premises, temporary festival tastings, and server training standards.

headings.title: Off-premises tasting samples without sales transactions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes wineries, distillers, brewers, and wholesalers to pour alcohol samples off licensed retail premises for tasting purposes provided no sales take place.

headings.title: Tasting samples at temporary licensed festival events
headings.reviewNote: Permits alcohol manufacturers and wholesalers to furnish and pour samples on temporary licensed retail premises and tax-exempt civic events.

headings.title: On-premises retail product tastings and server training
headings.reviewNote: Regulates tastings on retail premises, server training certification for pouring staff, prohibition of retailer compensation, and return of unused product.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.299 mandating display of pregnancy birth defect warning signs, supervisor violation notices, and criminal immunity.

headings.title: Mandatory pregnancy warning sign on licensed premises
headings.reviewNote: Requires retail liquor licensees to conspicuously display an 11-by-14-inch sign warning that drinking alcoholic beverages during pregnancy may cause birth defects.

headings.title: Inspection and notice of warning sign violation
headings.reviewNote: Permits any employee of the supervisor of liquor control to report a violation of this section, upon which the supervisor shall issue a warning to the licensee.

headings.title: Exemption from criminal liability for sign violation
headings.reviewNote: Provides that failure to display the required pregnancy warning sign does not constitute a criminal offense under chapter 311.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 311.300 governing age-18 employment permissions in package stores, warehouses, wholesale delivery, and restaurant food service.

headings.title: Prohibition on selling liquor under age twenty-one
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits persons under twenty-one years of age from selling or dispensing intoxicating liquor, except as provided by this section.

headings.title: Retail package store employment at age eighteen
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes persons aged eighteen or older to stock, ring up, and sack package liquor, requiring on-site supervision by a 21-year-old if food sales are under 50%.

headings.title: Distillery and warehouse employment at age eighteen
headings.reviewNote: Permits persons aged eighteen or older to be employed in distilleries, warehouses, and wholesale distributorships to handle liquor for non-retail purposes.

headings.title: Wholesale delivery and display stocking at age eighteen
headings.reviewNote: Allows wholesalers to employ persons aged eighteen or older to rotate displays and unload delivery vehicles under supervision of an adult driver.

headings.title: Waiters and waitresses serving liquor at age eighteen
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes persons aged eighteen or older working as restaurant servers to accept payment and serve liquor where food sales are at least 50%, prohibiting bartending.

entries.reviewSummary: Misdemeanor penalties for supplying alcohol to minors, intoxicated persons, or habitual drunkards, property owner liability for allowing underage drinking, and retail licensee photo-ID defense.

headings.title: Unlawful sale or supply to minor or drunkard
headings.reviewNote: Makes it a misdemeanor to sell or supply intoxicating liquor to a person under twenty-one, intoxicated person, or habitual drunkard, with medical exceptions.

headings.title: Permitting minor drinking or possession on property
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowingly permitting a person under twenty-one to possess or consume alcohol on private property as a class B misdemeanor, elevated to class A for repeat offenses.

headings.title: Photo-identification defense for licensed retailers and employees
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a defense to prosecution for a licensed retailer, club, drinking establishment, caterer, temporary permit holder, or employee who sold to a minor with reasonable cause based on an official or apparently official photo ID purporting to show age 21+.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.315 defining the offense of manufacturing false identification cards for minors and establishing class A misdemeanor penalties.

headings.title: Offense of manufacturing false identification for alcohol
headings.reviewNote: Defines the offense of manufacturing false identification as possessing means of identification for manufacturing or selling fake IDs to minors to obtain alcohol.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for false identification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies the offense of manufacturing a false identification card for underage alcohol acquisition as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.320 establishing penalties for age misrepresentation by minors and mandatory $500 fines for using altered identification documents.

headings.title: Misrepresentation of age by minor to obtain liquor
headings.reviewNote: Classifies age misrepresentation by persons aged seventeen to twenty to obtain liquor as a misdemeanor, and as juvenile delinquency for minors under seventeen.

headings.title: Use of altered driver license or identification
headings.reviewNote: Imposes a misdemeanor and $500 fine per offense (in addition to sub. 1 and sections 302.400 to 302.426, transferred from 577.500 to 577.530 per source footnote) on persons under 21 using altered/reproduced licenses, military IDs, passports, or state IDs to obtain liquor.

entries.reviewSummary: Minor purchase, possession, or intoxication misdemeanor penalties, sealed-container intoxicating liquor presumption, implied consent to chemical testing, and accredited college culinary-student tasting exemption.

headings.title: Minor purchase, possession, or intoxication penalties
headings.reviewNote: Classifies minor purchase, possession, visible intoxication, or blood alcohol content above 0.02% as a class D misdemeanor for first offense and class A for subsequent offenses.

headings.title: Presumption that sealed container contains intoxicating liquor
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a rebuttable presumption in administrative and judicial proceedings that a manufacturer-sealed labeled container contains intoxicating liquor without opening or testing.

headings.title: Implied consent to chemical testing for minors
headings.reviewNote: Deems an underage person suspected of purchasing, possessing, or consuming liquor to have consented to chemical breath, blood, or urine testing.

headings.title: Exemption for accredited college culinary course students
headings.reviewNote: Exempts students aged 18+ enrolled in accredited college/university culinary courses who taste (without consuming/imbibing) fermented beverages for required curriculum instruction under the possession and control of an authorized instructor aged 21+.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.328 establishing acceptable photographic identification forms, retailer good-faith defense, and criminal penalties for ID tampering.

headings.title: Acceptable forms of photographic identification
headings.reviewNote: Lists valid unexpired photographic IDs acceptable to verify age 21+ (Missouri or out-of-state operator's/chauffeur's license, Missouri or out-of-state nondriver's ID card, uniformed service ID, or passport) and requires comparing photo and physical characteristics.

headings.title: Good faith defense for compliant retail licensees
headings.reviewNote: Shields a licensee from administrative penalties upon proof of full compliance with identification check requirements and good-faith action.

headings.title: Criminal penalty for unauthorized reproduction of identification
headings.reviewNote: Makes unauthorized reproduction, alteration, or falsification of driver's licenses or state identification cards a misdemeanor punishable by up to $1,000 fine and one year confinement.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.332 prohibiting wholesale price discrimination, capping retailer discounts, and permitting donations to charitable auctions and churches.

headings.title: Wholesale price discrimination prohibited and discount limits
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits wholesalers from discriminating in price or discounts between retailers, capping quantity discounts at one percent and prompt-payment discounts at one percent.

headings.title: Donations of alcoholic beverages for charitable events
headings.reviewNote: Permits manufacturers and wholesalers to deliver nonresale beer, wine, or sacramental wine to charitable, religious, or educational organizations, requiring delivery logs.

headings.title: Original package donations for charitable fund-raising auctions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes donation of original package wine, beer, and spirits to religious or educational institutions for fundraising auctions and raffles on licensed retail premises.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.333 authorizing wholesale product returns and requiring monthly wholesale price schedules to be furnished to all retailers.

headings.title: Wholesaler acceptance of alcoholic beverage product returns
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes wholesalers to accept returns of intoxicating liquor and wine in accordance with administrative rules promulgated by the supervisor.

headings.title: Monthly wholesale pricing schedule furnished to retailers
headings.reviewNote: Requires wholesalers to furnish detailed monthly product price lists to all retailers at least five days prior to the first of the month, allowing immediate supplemental listings.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.335 governing wholesale delivery pricing, delayed shipment credit rules, and six-month close-out merchandise sales below cost.

headings.title: Delivery price tied to effective monthly schedule
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensed wholesalers to deliver intoxicating liquor and wine to retailers at the wholesale price in effect for the calendar month in which delivery occurs.

headings.title: Delayed shipments and month-end order procedures
headings.reviewNote: Regulates month-end orders and delayed shipments delivered within the first five business days of the subsequent month, deemed delivered on the last business day.

headings.title: Close-out merchandise sales below cost requirements
headings.reviewNote: Permits wholesalers to sell close-out merchandise below cost if identified on monthly price lists for at least six consecutive months, barring purchases during close-out.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.355 regulating manufacturer direct consumer cash rebate coupons and merchandise coupons redeemable without purchase.

headings.title: Consumer cash rebate coupons for intoxicating liquor
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes manufacturers of liquor other than beer to offer direct consumer cash rebate coupons advertised in media or distributed at retail point of sale.

headings.title: Non-purchase merchandise coupons for alcoholic beverages
headings.reviewNote: Permits manufacturers of beer, wine, and spirits to offer merchandise coupons redeemable without a purchase requirement, advertised in media or distributed at retail.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.360 prohibiting alcohol brand substitution and misrepresentation, with safe harbors for federally approved wine labels, noting commerce clause case law.

headings.title: Misrepresentation and brand substitution prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits licensees from selling or substituting intoxicating liquor of one manufacturer under the representation that it is the product of another, making violations a misdemeanor.

headings.title: Exception for wine with federal label approval
headings.reviewNote: Exempts wine and brandy sales from misrepresentation penalties if the manufacturer provided the supervisor with a federal TTB certificate of label approval.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.390 mandating common carriers to provide shipping receipts to the supervisor and establishing forfeiture collection actions.

headings.title: Carrier duty to furnish shipping records
headings.reviewNote: Requires common carriers and transportation companies to furnish duplicate bills of lading showing liquor shipments to the supervisor upon request, subject to a $50 fine per failure.

headings.title: Proceedings to recover carrier forfeiture penalties
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the supervisor and director of revenue to direct the attorney general or local prosecutors to initiate court proceedings to recover forfeitures for school funds.

entries.reviewSummary: Transporter's license ($10/yr or $5 single transaction) and $1,000 bond for transporting >5 gallons of liquor with carrier and licensee exemptions, character/liquor-conviction qualifications, and section 311.185 wine delivery carrier license requirement.

headings.title: Transporter license requirement and surety bond
headings.reviewNote: Requires a $10 annual ($5 single-transaction) transporter's license and $1,000 surety bond to transport >5 gallons of intoxicating liquor, exempting regulated carriers under chs. 387/389/390, Missouri-licensed premises, retail purchases, and industrial alcohol.

headings.title: Transporter license applicant qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Exempts transporter licenses from general chapter qualifications, requiring good moral character, no post-21st Amendment liquor manufacture/sale conviction, no revoked ATC license, and qualified corporate managing officers.

headings.title: Alcohol carrier license required for direct wine delivery
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits carriers licensed under or exempt from this section from delivering wine to a Missouri resident without obtaining an alcohol carrier license under section 311.185.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 311.480 governing unlicensed eating place consumption licenses (BYOB), operating hours, nuisance injunctions, and election day polling bars.

headings.title: Consumption license required for unlicensed eating establishments
headings.reviewNote: Requires operators of unlicensed food, beverage, or entertainment establishments to obtain a consumption-on-premises license before permitting patrons to drink alcohol.

headings.title: Application, annual fee, and renewal procedures
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an annual sixty-dollar consumption license fee expiring June 30th, monthly proration, and May 1st annual renewal deadline.

headings.title: Permitted consumption hours and municipal regulation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits drinking on premises by minors or between 1:30 a.m. and 6:00 a.m., establishes voter/taxpayer licensee qualifications, and allows municipal fees up to $300.

headings.title: Noncompliant consumption premises declared public nuisance
headings.reviewNote: Declares premises permitting unlawful alcohol consumption to be a public nuisance subject to injunction actions by prosecutors or the circuit attorney.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for knowing violation
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowing violations of consumption license rules by operators, employees, or partners as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Rulemaking, suspension, and revocation authority
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the supervisor of liquor control to promulgate administrative regulations and suspend or revoke consumption licenses for violations.

headings.title: Wholesale delivery rights preserved
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section does not prohibit licensed wholesalers from delivering intoxicating liquor to licensed retail dealers.

headings.title: Prohibition on service at election polling places
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits serving or selling intoxicating liquor on any premises used as a polling place on election day.

entries.reviewSummary: Temporary 7-day retail drink and package permits for churches and civic/charitable organizations, $25 fee without photo requirement, 6:00 a.m. Sunday sales, 15-day sales tax notice/penalties without bond, and wholesaler equipment.

headings.title: Temporary seven-day permit for civic and charitable groups
headings.reviewNote: Permits issuing a temporary permit (max 7 days) to a church, school, civic, service, fraternal, veteran, political, or charitable organization to sell all kinds of intoxicating liquor by the drink and in original packages at picnics, bazaars, or fairs.

headings.title: Application form without photograph and twenty-five-dollar fee
