headings.reviewNote: Requires completing a supervisor-provided form without requiring a personal photograph and paying a $25 fee for the permit.

headings.title: Sunday sales authorized beginning at 6:00 a.m.
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes sales of intoxicating liquor beginning at 6:00 a.m. if the permitted event is held on a Sunday.

headings.title: Sales tax notification, fifteen-day payment, and no bond
headings.reviewNote: Requires certified-mail notice to the director of revenue accepting sales tax responsibility, payment within 15 days after event close (triple-tax liability plus 3-year permit bar for nonpayment), and prohibits requiring a bond.

headings.title: Wholesaler storage, cooling, and dispensing equipment permitted
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that no law or rule prevents wholesalers or distributors from providing customary storage, cooling, or dispensing equipment to permit holders at such gatherings.

entries.reviewSummary: Temporary 168-hour ($10/day) festival permits for retail by-the-drink licensees, local ordinance compliance and package sales, 72-hour wholesaler unused-product credit, and customary equipment.

headings.title: Temporary festival permit for retail drink licensees
headings.reviewNote: Permits issuing a temporary festival (ch. 316) permit (<=168 consecutive hours, $10/calendar day, applied for >=5 business days prior) to retail by-the-drink licensees furnishing provisions and service.

headings.title: Application of local ordinances and original package sales
headings.reviewNote: Extends state liquor laws and municipal or county ordinances to the festival premises during operations and authorizes selling intoxicating liquor in the original package.

headings.title: Wholesaler credit for unused festival liquor within 72 hours
headings.reviewNote: Permits (without requiring) wholesalers to give retailers credit for unused intoxicating liquor delivered and invoiced under the permit if removed within 72 hours after permit expiration.

headings.title: Customary storage, cooling, and dispensing equipment permitted
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that no law or rule prevents wholesalers, retailers, or distributors from providing customary storage, cooling, or dispensing equipment for use at a festival.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 311.485 governing temporary $10/day catering permits, local compliance, statewide caterer deliveries, and 72-hour inventory returns.

headings.title: Temporary off-premises catering permit and daily fee
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes licensed retail drink dealers and caterers to obtain temporary off-premises permits for catered functions at ten dollars per day.

headings.title: Local ordinance compliance and package sales rights
headings.reviewNote: Subjects catered premises to municipal ordinances and allows caterers to sell intoxicating liquor in original packages.

headings.title: Statewide caterer delivery authority without extra licenses
headings.reviewNote: Permits caterers possessing valid state and local licenses to deliver alcoholic beverages statewide without separate municipal delivery licenses.

headings.title: Wholesaler credit for unused catered product returns
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes wholesalers to give credit for unused malt liquor under five percent alcohol removed within seventy-two hours of event expiration.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 311.486 establishing 50-day ($500) and unlimited ($1,000) annual catering licenses, 3-day notice, and delivery privileges.

headings.title: Fifty-day annual special catering license and fee
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes retail drink licensees and caterers to obtain an annual special catering license valid for up to fifty days per year for a $500 fee.

headings.title: Unlimited annual special catering license and fee
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes retail drink licensees and caterers to obtain an annual special catering license for an unlimited number of catered events for a $1,000 fee.

headings.title: Advance notice requirement for catered event locations
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual catering licensees to report each function location to the supervisor three business days in advance with property owner and city approvals.

headings.title: Application of liquor laws and package sales
headings.reviewNote: Applies all state and municipal liquor laws to catered premises and authorizes original package sales at catered events.

headings.title: Caterer delivery rights across municipal boundaries
headings.reviewNote: Permits licensed caterers to deliver alcoholic beverages in the course of business without separate municipal licenses where permitted by the destination city.

headings.title: Wholesaler product credit for unused catered inventory
headings.reviewNote: Permits wholesalers to accept returns and issue credit for unused low-alcohol malt liquor removed within seventy-two hours of function expiration.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.487 governing annual beer and Missouri wine licenses for state fair concessionaires and extending municipal jurisdiction.

headings.title: State fair concessionaire beer and wine licenses
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes annual licenses for state fair concessionaires to sell malt liquor and Missouri wines on the fairgrounds for $100 ($300 for grandstand and exhibition center).

headings.title: Extension of municipal ordinances to fairgrounds premises
headings.reviewNote: Extends all state liquor control laws and Sedalia municipal ordinances to licensed premises on the state fairgrounds during operations.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.510 governing supervisor inspection of malt liquors, sample testing exemptions for TTB-approved beers, and in-state label rules.

headings.title: Supervisor duty to inspect malt liquor purity
headings.reviewNote: Directs the supervisor of liquor control to inspect all beer brewed or sold in Missouri to ensure wholesome ingredients and correct labeling.

headings.title: Testing exemption upon federal label approval
headings.reviewNote: Bars the supervisor from requiring product samples or alcohol-content testing for beer or malt liquor upon receiving a copy of a federal Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau (source footnote notes 'Alcohol and Tobacco Trade Bureau' in original rolls) certificate of label approval.

headings.title: State authority over in-state beer product labels
headings.reviewNote: Grants the supervisor sole authority to approve labels for beer brewed and sold exclusively in Missouri without requiring federal TTB approval.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 311.520 governing malt liquor barrel inspection fees, American vs foreign import rate changes in 2026, and 2-year invoice retention.

headings.title: Definitions of American brewery and foreign import
headings.reviewNote: Defines American brewery and foreign import malt liquor for statutory inspection and gauging charge classifications.

headings.title: Pre-2026 barrel inspection charge for malt liquors
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director of revenue to collect an inspection and gauging fee of one dollar and eighty-six cents per barrel for tax years ending on or before December 31, 2025.

headings.title: Tiered barrel inspection fees beginning 2026
headings.reviewNote: Establishes barrel inspection charges of sixty-two cents for American-brewed malt liquors and one dollar and eighty-six cents for foreign import malt liquors starting January 1, 2026.

headings.title: Duplicate invoice and country of origin records
headings.reviewNote: Requires manufacturers and wholesalers to retain duplicate invoices showing shipment dates, quantities, and foreign origin country for two years.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for malt inspection fees
headings.reviewNote: Grants the director of revenue and supervisor rulemaking authority under chapter 536 with nonseverability provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.540 establishing inspection and gauging mandates for distilled spirits, and sample testing exemptions for federally approved labels.

headings.title: Inspection, gauging, and labeling of spirituous liquors
headings.reviewNote: Requires manufacturers, distillers, and importers of spirituous liquors to submit products to the supervisor of liquor control for inspection, gauging, and label verification.

headings.title: Sample testing exemption upon federal ATF approval
headings.reviewNote: Bars the supervisor from requiring product samples or alcohol-content testing for spirituous liquors if provided a copy of a certificate of label approval from the Federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms verifying alcohol content.

entries.reviewSummary: Additional revenue charges on spirituous liquors ($2/gal) and wines ($0.21/gal to Agriculture Protection Fund, eff. 7-01-26), first-seller liability and sales tax refund bar, nonpayment felony, container reuse misdemeanor, 2-year duplicate invoices, and unlicensed-sale felony.

headings.title: Revenue charges on spirituous liquors and wine
headings.reviewNote: Imposes additional revenue charges of $2.00 per gallon on spirituous liquors and $0.21 per gallon on wines (credited to the section 261.200 Agriculture Protection Fund; effective 7-01-26).

headings.title: First-seller liability and chapter 144 refund bar
headings.reviewNote: Makes the first seller in Missouri liable for payment and bars chapter 144 sales tax refund claims for retail sales tax erroneously collected on amounts representing chapter 311 charges under sections 311.520, 311.550, and 311.554.

headings.title: Felony penalty for selling untaxed spirituous liquor
headings.reviewNote: Makes selling spirituous liquors under subsection 1(1) without paying the required charge a felony punishable by 2–5 years DOC, 1 month–1 year county jail, $50–$1,000 fine, or both.

headings.title: Container destruction requirement and refilling misdemeanor
headings.reviewNote: Makes removing contents of a spirituous liquor container without destroying it, or refilling such container in whole or part, a misdemeanor.

headings.title: Two-year retention of duplicate shipment invoices
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensed manufacturers, out-state solicitors, and wholesalers to make and retain true duplicate shipment/delivery invoices for two years subject to ATC inspection.

headings.title: Felony penalty for unlicensed sale of intoxicating liquor
headings.reviewNote: Makes selling intoxicating liquor in Missouri without first procuring an ATC license a felony punishable by 2–5 years DOC, 3 months–1 year county jail, $100–$1,000 fine, or both.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.553 establishing monthly sworn tax return deadlines, supervisor authority for interim returns, and late deficiency penalties.

headings.title: Monthly sworn returns and payment by fifteenth day
headings.reviewNote: Requires manufacturers, out-of-state solicitors, and wholesalers to file sworn monthly reports and remit excise charges by the fifteenth day of each month.

headings.title: Supervisor authority to require more frequent returns
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the supervisor of liquor control to mandate returns covering periods shorter than a month to secure payment of state revenue charges.

headings.title: Late payment penalty and interest charges
headings.reviewNote: Imposes a penalty of one percent per business day (up to 25%) and interest at one percent per month on delinquent revenue charges until paid.

entries.reviewSummary: Two additional 10.5-cent per-gallon wine revenue charges (eff. 7-01-26) deposited in the nonreverting Missouri Wine and Grape Fund exclusively for Missouri grape and wine market development.

headings.title: Additional revenue charge on sale of wine
headings.reviewNote: Levies an additional state revenue charge of ten and one-half cents per gallon on the privilege of selling wine in Missouri.

headings.title: Allocation of wine proceeds to grape fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs subsection 1 proceeds (formerly to the Marketing Development Fund—renamed Agriculture Business Development Fund per 2008 footnote—through June 30, 2006) to the Missouri Wine and Grape Fund solely for Missouri grape/wine market development, viticulture, and enology.

headings.title: Creation and administration of wine and grape fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri Wine and Grape Fund as a dedicated, nonreverting state treasury fund administered by the department of agriculture.

headings.title: Second additional ten-and-one-half-cent wine charge
headings.reviewNote: Imposes a second additional 10.5-cent per-gallon wine charge (in addition to sub. 1 and section 311.550) deposited in the Missouri Wine and Grape Fund (formerly Marketing Development Fund through June 30, 2006; effective 7-01-26).

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibition on possessing unlawfully manufactured liquor in any quantity and untaxed/unlicensed liquor for sale or over five gallons, with exceptions for bulk manufacturing and U.S. bonded warehouses.

headings.title: Possession of unlawfully manufactured liquor prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any person from possessing intoxicating liquor in any quantity for any purpose in Missouri that has not been lawfully manufactured.

headings.title: Untaxed liquor possession ban and bonded warehouse exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits possessing liquor for sale in any quantity, or for other purposes over five gallons, without paying required fees/license, with exemptions for licensed manufacturers' bulk stock and U.S. internal revenue or customs bonded warehouses.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 311.610 establishing the appointment, full-time duties, staffing, surety bond, and annual reporting of the supervisor of liquor control.

headings.title: Appointment of supervisor by governor
headings.reviewNote: Provides for appointment of the supervisor of liquor control by the governor with senate advice and consent, serving at the governor's pleasure.

headings.title: Full-time service, staff appointments, and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Requires full-time devotion to office duties, authorizes hiring enforcement agents with an $8,000 minimum salary, and provides expense reimbursements.

headings.title: Official constitutional oath and surety bond
headings.reviewNote: Requires the supervisor to take a constitutional oath and execute an approved $10,000 official surety bond to the state of Missouri.

headings.title: License issuance duties and annual report to governor
headings.reviewNote: Directs the supervisor to issue liquor licenses, maintain statewide production and distribution records, and submit annual reports to the governor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 311.620 detailing qualification standards, political activity prohibitions, surety bonds, and mandatory dismissal for liquor control agents.

headings.title: Qualifications for liquor control agents and inspectors
headings.reviewNote: Establishes qualifications for division agents: U.S. citizenship, Missouri resident taxpayer status, literacy, physical fitness, character, and no pending indictments.

headings.title: Prohibition on outside employment, gifts, and electioneering
headings.reviewNote: Bars division agents from holding outside office or employment without permission, accepting gifts, or participating in political campaigns or electioneering.

headings.title: Official oath and five thousand dollar surety bond
headings.reviewNote: Requires all appointed agents and inspectors to take an official oath and execute a five thousand dollar faithful-performance surety bond paid by the state.

headings.title: Immediate discharge for statutory violations
headings.reviewNote: Mandates immediate dismissal for any agent, assistant, deputy, or inspector of the division who violates provisions of this chapter.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.630 establishing peace officer status for liquor control agents, credentials, badges, and arrest fee taxation.

headings.title: Peace officer status and statutory arrest powers
headings.reviewNote: Designates the supervisor and qualified division agents as state peace officers authorized to make arrests and searches for liquor and tobacco violations.

headings.title: Official credentials, special badge, and public roster
headings.reviewNote: Directs the supervisor to furnish designated peace officers with official credentials and badges, maintaining a public record of their names.

headings.title: Arrest and service fees taxed as costs
headings.reviewNote: Provides that statutory fees for arrests, prisoner transportation, and process service by division peace officers shall be taxed as court costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.660 detailing supervisor regulatory, licensing, inspection, and subpoena powers, and limiting employee felony disqualifications.

headings.title: Regulatory, rulemaking, and subpoena powers of supervisor
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the supervisor to suspend/revoke licenses, regulate package capacities, labels, and licensee conduct, inspect books, issue subpoenas, and administer oaths.

headings.title: Felony conviction restriction on employment rules
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the supervisor from barring individuals from employment in alcohol sales solely on the basis of felony convictions, subject to vintage wine exceptions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.665 requiring sales and use tax clearance from the director of revenue for liquor license renewal.

headings.title: Tax clearance statement required for renewal
headings.reviewNote: Requires the supervisor to obtain a statement from the director of revenue verifying payment of all sales and use taxes prior to license renewal.

headings.title: Filing deadline for tax clearance statement
headings.reviewNote: Directs the licensee to file a copy of the issued sales and use tax statement with the supervisor within ten days.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 311.680 establishing disciplinary sanctions, capacity-tiered civil penalties, and conference procedures for disorderly premises.

headings.title: Disciplinary authority for disorderly premises
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the supervisor to issue warnings, impose probation up to twelve months, or suspend or revoke licenses for disorderly premises or violations.

headings.title: Civil penalties assessed against wholesalers
headings.reviewNote: Permits the supervisor to assess civil penalties between one hundred and twenty-five hundred dollars per violation against licensed wholesalers.

headings.title: Civil penalties assessed against solicitors
headings.reviewNote: Permits the supervisor to assess civil penalties or fines between one hundred and five thousand dollars per violation against licensed solicitors.

headings.title: Civil penalties for smaller retailers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes civil penalties between fifty and one thousand dollars per violation for retailers with occupant capacity under five thousand.

headings.title: Civil penalties for large-capacity retailers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes civil penalties between fifty and five thousand dollars per violation for retailers with occupant capacity of five thousand or more.

headings.title: Administrative hearing commission appeal rights
headings.reviewNote: Provides that any aggrieved person may appeal supervisory disciplinary decisions to the administrative hearing commission under section 311.691.

headings.title: Pre-order meet and confer opportunity
headings.reviewNote: Requires offering a meet-and-confer opportunity with at least ten days' prior notice, written conduct description, citations, and requested documents before issuing discipline, with orders effective no sooner than thirty days from issuance.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.685 authorizing licensee civil damages actions against proximate violators and immunizing state and local enforcement personnel.

headings.title: Licensee civil action against proximate causes
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes retail licensees aggrieved by official actions to recover up to five thousand dollars in damages plus attorney fees from persons proximately causing violations.

headings.title: Immunity for state and local officers
headings.reviewNote: Bars civil actions under this section against employees of the supervisor of alcohol and tobacco control or law enforcement officers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 10 subsections for 311.710 establishing citizen complaint mechanisms, notice requirements, de novo bench hearings, and judicial license revocation.

headings.title: Citizen and officer retail complaints grounds
headings.reviewNote: Permits peace officers or eight taxpaying citizens to initiate circuit court proceedings for specified retail liquor license violations.

headings.title: Written sworn complaint submission procedure
headings.reviewNote: Requires taxpaying citizens to mail a sworn joint complaint to the supervisor and wait thirty days before filing in circuit court.

headings.title: Certification of administrative record on grievance
headings.reviewNote: Requires the supervisor to certify complaints and hearing transcripts to the circuit court without operating as a stay of administrative orders.

headings.title: Notice and scheduling of judicial hearing
headings.reviewNote: Directs the circuit clerk to schedule an early hearing and provide at least fifteen days' notice to the prosecutor and licensee.

headings.title: Bench trial and de novo proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that the circuit court conducts a non-jury hearing de novo allowing presentation of new and additional evidence.

headings.title: Judicial suspension or revocation orders
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the court to suspend or revoke retail licenses upon finding proven offenses while considering supervisory administrative orders.

headings.title: No stay during appellate review
headings.reviewNote: Provides that circuit court judgments revoking or suspending licenses shall not be superseded or stayed during appeal.

headings.title: Prosecutorial duty to pursue citizen complaints
headings.reviewNote: Directs prosecuting attorneys and circuit attorneys to prosecute citizen complaint proceedings diligently and without delay.

headings.title: Non-exclusive concurrent circuit court jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Preserves the supervisory authority of alcohol and tobacco control and establishes that judicial remedies are supplemental.

headings.title: Taxation of circuit court hearing costs
headings.reviewNote: Requires that costs accruing from circuit court complaint proceedings be taxed in the same manner as criminal costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 311.722 establishing standards, appearance rules, supervisor limitations, and liability exemptions for minors used in compliance investigations.

headings.title: Rulemaking condition for minor enforcement usage
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the supervisor from using minors in liquor law enforcement unless formal standards and regulations are promulgated.

headings.title: Permissive standards for minor investigative stings
headings.reviewNote: Establishes age, appearance, truthful identification, and conduct criteria for minors utilized in law enforcement compliance checks.

headings.title: Non-participation where standards not followed
headings.reviewNote: Bars the supervisor from participating or disciplining establishments when local agencies fail to follow promulgated minor investigative standards.

headings.title: Exemption from liability for participating minors
headings.reviewNote: Exempts minors acting under direct law enforcement control from statutory liquor violations during investigative operations.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.730 allocating seventy percent of liquor permit fees to the division fund and the remainder to general revenue.

headings.title: General revenue deposit of collected fees
headings.reviewNote: Requires liquor license, inspection, and gauging fees to be credited to the ordinary state revenue fund except as dedicated.

headings.title: Allocation to division dedicated fund
headings.reviewNote: Allocates seventy percent of license and permit fees collected under this chapter to the division of alcohol and tobacco control fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.735 creating the dedicated division of alcohol and tobacco control fund and prohibiting biennial reversion.

headings.title: Establishment and dedicated use of fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the division of alcohol and tobacco control fund in the state treasury solely for regulatory and licensing administration.

headings.title: Non-reversion of biennial fund balances
headings.reviewNote: Exempts unexpended biennial balances in the division fund from reverting to the credit of the general revenue fund.

headings.title: Legislative appropriations supporting division functions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that appropriations made by the general assembly from the fund shall be used to support the division of alcohol and tobacco control for subsection 1 purposes.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.740 classifying illegal liquor establishments as common nuisances, establishing misdemeanor penalties, and creating property liens.

headings.title: Declaration of unlawful premises as nuisance
headings.reviewNote: Declares places and equipment used for unlawful liquor manufacturing or sales to be common nuisances and establishes misdemeanor penalties.

headings.title: Owner liability and lien against premises
headings.reviewNote: Imposes a lien against property used for illegal liquor operations when permitted by the owner after having knowledge or reason to believe.

headings.title: Release of lien upon judgment satisfaction
headings.reviewNote: Provides that property liens are released upon entry of final judgment assessing no fines or full payment of assessed fines and costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.750 governing equity actions brought by public prosecutors to enjoin liquor nuisances and order premises closures.

headings.title: Injunction actions brought by state attorneys
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the attorney general, prosecuting attorneys, or circuit attorneys to initiate equity suits for temporary and permanent nuisance injunctions.

headings.title: Judicial abatement and premises closure orders
headings.reviewNote: Empowers courts upon proving material allegations to abate liquor nuisances and prohibit premises occupation for up to one year.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 311.770 defining prosecuting attorney nuisance duties, charging rules, and attorney general intervention upon prosecutorial default.

headings.title: Prosecutorial duty following criminal disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Requires prosecuting attorneys to promptly initiate nuisance abatement proceedings whenever unlawful liquor premises are revealed in criminal cases.

headings.title: Joinder of counts and charging standards
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes joinder of multiple liquor offenses in separate counts for single trial and specifies simplified charging language.

headings.title: Attorney general enforcement upon prosecutor default
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that the attorney general appoint assistants and enforce liquor laws in counties where local prosecutors fail or refuse to act.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.780 governing monthly transmissions of liquor complaints and suspensions and quarterly prosecutorial reporting.

headings.title: Monthly complaint and disciplinary transmission
headings.reviewNote: Requires the supervisor to send monthly lists of complaints, revocations, and suspensions to local prosecutors and the attorney general.

headings.title: Quarterly prosecutorial action reports
headings.reviewNote: Directs circuit attorneys and prosecuting attorneys to report quarterly on actions taken regarding transmitted complaints.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.790 establishing prosecution duties, attorney general representation, and civil recovery suits for delinquent liquor fees.

headings.title: Prosecution authority and attorney general representation
headings.reviewNote: Directs local prosecutors and the attorney general to investigate, prosecute liquor law violations, and represent the supervisor.

headings.title: Civil suits to recover delinquent charges
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes civil actions by prosecuting attorneys or the attorney general to recover unpaid liquor taxes, fees, and charges.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.810 detailing search warrant applications, property seizures, contraband forfeiture, and warrantless arrests.

headings.title: Application petition for search warrant
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the attorney general, prosecutors, the supervisor, or inspectors to apply for search warrants upon verified petition.

headings.title: Warrant execution seizure and contraband forfeiture
headings.reviewNote: Governs warrant execution, entry, seizure of liquor and manufacturing equipment, contraband status, warrantless arrests, and sale proceeds.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 311.840 establishing circuit court contraband forfeiture procedures, newspaper publication, innocent owner protections, and sales.

headings.title: Circuit court forfeiture petition and summons
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing a circuit court petition against the possessor for seized property over fifty dollars, establishing a rebuttable ownership presumption.

headings.title: Newspaper publication notice to interested parties
headings.reviewNote: Mandates one-time newspaper publication of seizure notice allowing interested claimants thirty days to assert property rights.

headings.title: Intervention deadline for property claimants
headings.reviewNote: Permits any person claiming an interest in seized property to intervene within thirty days following newspaper publication.

headings.title: Judicial relief for innocent owners and liens
headings.reviewNote: Governs court determinations restoring property to innocent owners, satisfying bona fide liens, or forfeiting contraband to general revenue.

headings.title: Appeals from circuit court forfeiture judgments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes appeals from circuit court forfeiture judgments in the same manner as other civil actions.

headings.title: Affixing excise stamps upon judicial sale
headings.reviewNote: Requires selling officers to procure and affix proper excise stamps from the director of revenue reimbursed through sale proceeds.

headings.title: Officer immunity from costs and storage
headings.reviewNote: Provides that officers commencing forfeiture actions on behalf of the state shall not be liable for costs or storage.

headings.title: Prosecutorial legal representation for seizing officers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes seizing officers and the supervisor to require representation by local prosecutors or the attorney general in forfeiture proceedings.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 311.850 governing sixty-day replevin suits, officer immunity, excise stamping, and default turnover for property under fifty dollars.

headings.title: Replevin action for low-value property
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes property claimants to file replevin within sixty days for seized property valued at fifty dollars or less with officer immunity.

headings.title: Appeals in low-value replevin proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Allows appeals from replevin court judgments in the same manner as other civil actions.

headings.title: Default turnover excise stamping and sale
headings.reviewNote: Directs turnover to the supervisor for stamping and sale into general revenue if no replevin suit is filed within sixty days.

headings.title: Prosecutorial representation in replevin actions
headings.reviewNote: Empowers seizing officers to call upon county prosecutors, the circuit attorney, or the attorney general for legal representation.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 311.868 providing that graduated administrative fines supersede other statutory penalties against manufacturers and distillers.

headings.title: Exclusive statutory penalties for manufacturers
headings.reviewNote: Provides that manufacturers and distillers are subject exclusively to specific monetary fines regarding their licenses in lieu of other penalties.

headings.title: Graduated fine schedule for violations
headings.reviewNote: Establishes fines of ten thousand dollars for first offenses, twenty-five thousand for second offenses, and fifty thousand for subsequent offenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 311.950 permitting mobile app alcohol purchases at entertainment venues, requiring ID verification, and establishing rules.

headings.title: Mobile application purchases at entertainment facilities
headings.reviewNote: Permits licensed entertainment facilities (arenas, stadiums) and concessionaires to sell and deliver alcoholic beverages purchased through mobile applications in compliance with state law (source note: 2016 S.B. 994 veto override effective 10-14-16).

headings.title: Definition of mobile application
headings.reviewNote: Defines mobile application as a computer program or software designed for hand-held devices including mobile phones and tablet computers.

headings.title: Mandatory photo identification age verification
headings.reviewNote: Requires concession employees delivering mobile-ordered beverages to verify government-issued photo identification confirming age twenty-one or older.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes administrative rulemaking under chapter 536 and specifies nonseverability conditions if legislative review powers are invalidated.
